 Home Alert Could PA see a $15 minimum wage? Could PA see a $15 minimum wage?
 Mon, November 9, 2026 by Staff Report 
 SHARE NOW 
 Pennsylvania could be moving closer to its first minimum wage increase in more than 17 years, following recent election results that will give Democrats control of both chambers of the state legislature.
 Gov. Josh Shapiro and Democratic legislative leaders say raising the minimum wage will be a priority when the new legislative session begins in January.
 Pennsylvania’s minimum wage currently stands at $7.25 an hour, the same as the federal minimum. The rate has not increased since 2009.
 Shapiro has repeatedly called for raising the minimum wage to $15 an hour. Following the November election, he said the increase would be the first bill he signs in January.
 A previous proposal, House Bill 2189, would gradually increase the minimum wage to $11 an hour in 2027, $13 in 2028 and $15 in 2029. It would also provide for annual cost-of-living adjustments. The legislation passed the state House in March but stalled in the Senate.
 Democratic lawmakers are now preparing another effort to increase the minimum wage during the 2027 legislative session. State Sen. Art Haywood says lawmakers believe the political obstacles that prevented previous increases have changed.
 However, business representatives have raised concerns about the potential effects of higher wages on small businesses, nonprofits and employment costs.
 The details of a new proposal, including the amount of the increase and when it would take effect, have not yet been finalized.
 Attorney Clint Barkdoll said, “I would say this is almost certain, and we would always hesitate to say that in in political things. But Governor Shapiro did several interviews over the weekend, again confirm that this is going to be likely House Bill Number One when they return in January, and it is looking like $15 an hour. And I’ve been advising my small business clients, the nonprofits, be ready for this because they’re getting their 2027 budgets ready now, and this is really going to hit some of those organizations. So that’s going to be item number one. There were some numbers I saw published over the weekend that it’s estimated that there are about half a million Pennsylvanians workers that would be under this $15 per hour minimum wage, and then there’s like another 400,000 that are just above it. So roughly, you’re talking 900,000 workers that one way or another would be directly affected by this, and it’s going to have a very big impact on budgets for small businesses and nonprofits.”
